Questions.content: What is the significance of having a 1 after and before the number in the context of the equation? This seems to imply placing the digit 1 in two different positions, which should be explicitly defined in the TG.

Answers.content:
In the context of the equation, having a 1 after the number means appending the digit 1 to the end of the five-digit number. This can be represented mathematically as multiplying the original number by 10 and then adding 1.

Having a 1 before the number means placing the digit 1 at the beginning of the five-digit number. Since it's a five-digit number, this effectively shifts all digits one place to the right and inserts 1 at the start. This can be represented as \(10^4 \times 1 + \text{original number}\), or simply \(10000 + \text{original number}\).

These two different placements of the digit 1 lead to the equation where appending 1 to the end makes the number three times what placing 1 at the beginning does. This setup is crucial for formulating the correct algebraic expression and solving for the unknown five-digit number.
